I'll be conservative: treat "reports pipeline" as a new entity and add the constraint about it. The fact "The reports pipeline must stay on Python 3.11 until the pandas 3 upgrade lands" is a durable constraint.

I think adding an alias is defensible but risky. The guidelines say don't invent anything. Aliasing "reports pipeline" to "reporting service" is an inference. Given ambiguity, I'll add it as its own entity "reports pipeline". That's the safest — the fact stands alone naming its subject.

Actually, let me reconsider. The memory system benefits from aliasing when the note clearly refers to the same thing. "Reports pipeline" vs "reporting service" — these could plausibly be the same, but "pipeline" is a distinct technical artifact. I'll keep them separate.
